title: Last Ninja Remix
build: The Force's crack of the 1990 disk, with Ikari+Talent's trainer, its two options left off (archive.org; side A SHA-1 5597c4896f0a6ada501fb13ad94359063a8c1e29, side B 22f881cff073a4797580f95ca6225903a0bfaa99): all seven levels

records.c: JMP $7A3B: the load coordinator jumps here ($1728, jmp $3FF3) once the play load is in, and this goes on to EngineEntry at $7A3B.

JMP $8113, an RTS in The Sewers' play load. This is the vector StartLevelLoad calls ($1405, jsr $3FF6) before it loads a part, but StartLevelLoad runs only once, when the game starts and before Central Park's first load, while the vector still holds the engine's own JMP $0E00 to the machine set-up. A finished level jumps to CoordinateLevelLoad at $16AD directly ($7C0D), past that call, so nothing calls this vector while this load is in memory.

The tune's restart flag: the interrupt routine restarts the tune (jsr $4000) when it finds this byte nonzero, clearing it first ($1EEE-$1EF8), and the title sequence clears it at $110D before it starts the tune. The six zero bytes after it, up to the music jumps at $4000, are read by no instruction.
JMP $40C4: the tune's start. The title sequence calls it at $1110 before it plays the tune, and the interrupt routine at $1EF8 when MusicRestartRequest asks for a restart.

JMP $4129: one step of the tune. The interrupt routine calls it at $1F0E on its raster interrupt, once a frame, while the music switch $AA is nonzero, except that while $AB is zero it leaves out every sixth; the title sequence calls it at $111D once a frame, timed by the raster.
JMP $411F: stores A in the player's three control bytes, $4050, $4051 and $4052.

JMP $422F: adds one to $404B. While that byte is not zero the tick routine does not play: it writes the byte to the three voices' control registers ($D404, $D40B, $D412) and the player's control bytes, and returns.
61 bytes of text that nothing reads, carried with the tune: "COOL REMIX BY REYN OUWEHAND AND PLAYER/SOUNDS BY FALCO PAUL".

The body of MusicInit, which the JMP at $4000 reaches with the song number in A, and the start of the player's code. It multiplies A by eight to index the song table at $4A4B, copies the song's first two bytes into the tempo reloads $404E and $404F, and sets the volume $4054 to 15. For each of the three voices it copies the playlist pointer into $4076 and $4079, sets the duration countdown $4055 to 1, and clears the playlist place $4073, the phrase place $4070, the repeat count $407C, the instrument base $4061, the transpose $406D and the pulse-width switch $40C0; $404D is set to 1. It then clears the filter switch $40C3, the filter mode bits $4053, the tick divider $404C and the gate $404B, writes zero to the three voices' control registers ($D404, $D40B, $D412) and to $4050-$4052, and returns. Clobbers: A, X, Y and flags.

Implement Level's $4006 music-control veneer by storing A into the module's three control bytes and returning.
Inputs: A is the control value; the matching retained music occupant and its writable state are active.
Outputs: A is stored to $4050-$4052; A, X, Y, and all status flags are preserved on return.
Clobbers: Memory $4050-$4052; A, X, Y, and flags are preserved, and RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Hardware: No hardware registers are written directly.
Copy A into the paired global music-control bytes. Inputs: A is the control value. Outputs: both control bytes equal A; A, X, Y, and flags are preserved. Clobbers: memory only.

Implement Level's $4003 music-tick veneer, honoring the module gate and advancing its sequencer and SID image.
Inputs: The module is initialized; $404B is its gate byte and the resident IRQ enters through the matching $4003 veneer.
Outputs: Advances or gates the current music tick, updates sequencer/envelope state, emits the resulting SID register values, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, zero-page music cursors, module track/envelope state, and SID register state.
Hardware: Writes SID voice and filter/volume registers as directed by the current tick; no CIA or VIC-II access is introduced by the veneer body.

Implement Level's $4009 gate veneer by incrementing the module gate byte and returning.
Inputs: $404B is the writable gate byte for the matching retained music occupant.
Outputs: $404B is incremented modulo 256; N and Z describe the new value; A, X, and Y are preserved.
Clobbers: $404B, N, and Z; A, X, Y, C, V, D, and I are preserved, and RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Hardware: No hardware registers are written directly.

Steps the instrument's waveform list and pitch list for voice X, once a tick; the tick routine calls it at $4457 for an instrument whose byte 7 has bit 7 set. Byte 1 of the instrument ($496D, with the record offset from $4067 in Y) is the number of both lists: it is written into the operand of the LDY at $4576 and picks the waveform list's pointer from $4949 and $494B. The first time it runs for a note ($405B still zero) both list places, $4082 and $4085, are cleared. The waveform list's byte at the place goes to $407F, the voice's waveform and gate byte, and the place moves on; $FE leaves both as they are, and $FF is followed by the place to go to, whose byte is used. It then goes on into the pitch list at $4576. Clobbers: A, Y, flags and $FE/$FF; X is kept.

records.s: [offcut 4564] Self-modified immediate operand of `LDY #$00` at `$4576`. The Sewers music sequencer writes the selected sequence index here at `$4544`; the following indexed table reads install the sequence pointer in `$FE/$FF`.

records.c: The operand of the LDY #$00 at $4576, which the instruction at $4544, earlier in the same routine, rewrites: with the voice's instrument number from $4067 it reads the instrument's byte in the table at $496D, stores it here, and the LDY then loads it, the number of the instrument's pitch sequence.

Loads the selected four-entry pitch-sequence pointer, reads the current per-voice cursor $4085, handles $FD/$FE control and $FF redirection, updates frequency-high state $4094, clears $4091 and advances the cursor. The $45A5 branch advances the cursor then restores the note frequency through $45D6. Uses the instrument-selected index embedded in the preceding LDY operand.

One tick of voice X's arpeggio, called at $444F when the voice's arpeggio number $408B is nonzero and bit 4 of the instrument's flags is clear. Y is the arpeggio number: it picks the list's pointer from $48FA and $4900. The place $408E moves on one byte; that byte is added to the note $406A as a signed number of semitones and the voice's frequency is set to that note's ($45D6). $80 leaves the place and the frequency as they are, and $81 is followed by the place to go to, whose byte is used. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $FE/$FF, the place $408E and the frequency $4091/$4094; X is kept.

Set the voice's frequency to a note's. Inputs: Y is the note number and X the voice. Outputs: the low and high bytes from $483B,Y and $489B,Y go to $4091,X and $4094,X, the frequency the tick writes to the voice's $D400/$D401. Clobbers: A and flags.

One tick of a slide for voice X (set up by a phrase's $FB-$FE command), called at $43F9 once the note's tick count $405B reaches the slide's start $4097. Inputs: Y is the slide speed from $409A; the step is four times it, a 16-bit amount in $FE/$FF. If the target note $409D is at or above the note $406A the step is added to the voice's frequency $4091/$4094, otherwise subtracted. Outputs: once the frequency goes past the target note's, it is set to that note's ($45D6), the speed $409A and $40A9 are cleared and the target becomes the voice's note $406A. Clobbers: A, Y, flags and $FE/$FF; X is kept.

One tick of voice X's vibrato, called at $4411 once the note's tick count $405B reaches the setting's byte 0. Inputs: Y is the vibrato setting's offset, half the instrument's byte 9. The first run for a note ($40A9 zero) only works out the depth, the frequency difference between the note $406A and the note byte 4 above it, halved as many times as byte 5 says, into $40A3/$40A6, clears the list place $40A0 and sets $40A9. Later runs add byte 6 to the depth while the tick count is at least byte 1 and below byte 7, set the frequency back to the note's ($45D6) and step the up-and-down list that bytes 2 and 3 point at: a byte from 1 to $7F adds the depth that many times, 0 adds nothing, $81 is followed by the place to go to, and any other byte with bit 7 set subtracts it 256 minus that many times; the place moves on. Clobbers: A, Y, flags and $FE/$FF; X is kept.

Conditionally initialize one voice's modulation stream. Inputs: X selects the voice, Y selects its modulation definition, and the current per-voice guard controls initialization. Outputs: when the guard is zero, the modulation cursor and count are cleared and the definition's mode bit is installed; otherwise voice state is unchanged. Clobbers: A and flags, plus indexed voice state only on the initialization path; X and Y are preserved.

One step of voice X's pulse-width sweep (X 0 to 2), or of the filter cut-off when X is 3 (the call at $443D). Y is the instrument's setting, an offset into the filter and pulse settings: their bytes 6 and 7 point at the sweep list, whose entries set the voice's 16-bit value ($40B0 high, $40AC low) outright or start a run of steps, and the settings' steps move the value up or down between two limits. The frequency is not touched. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $FE/$FF, $404A and the voice's place and count in the list ($40B8, $40BC).
0, 7, 14: the offset of each voice's registers from $D400, which the player adds to every SID register address it writes for that voice.
1, 2, 4: each voice's bit in the filter routing, which the player adds to the routing byte it writes to $D417 when an instrument switches the filter on.
23 multiples of eleven, 0 to 242: an instrument command in a phrase adds its number to the voice's instrument base and looks up here the offset of that instrument's eleven-byte record.
Low bytes of the SID frequency for each of the 96 notes, lowest first, read with the note number in Y.
High bytes of the frequencies, read with the same note number. Only 95 are stored: the next table starts where the high byte of the top note would be.

Low bytes of arpeggio pointers 0 to 5, chosen by the number in a phrase's $E0-$F7 command. Pointer 6's low byte is the first byte of the high table after it ($4900), which is also pointer 0's high byte: the two tables overlap by a byte. Pointer 0 ($3FFD) is never followed, since the player skips the arpeggio when the number is 0.
High bytes of arpeggio pointers 0 to 6: $3FFD, $4907, $4910, $4919, $4921, $4935, $493F.

Arpeggio list, $4907-$490F: every tick the player steps to the next byte and adds it to the note as a signed number of semitones, so the voice cycles through a chord; $80 holds the current step, and $81 is followed by the position to go back to.

Arpeggio list, $4910-$4918: every tick the player steps to the next byte and adds it to the note as a signed number of semitones, so the voice cycles through a chord; $80 holds the current step, and $81 is followed by the position to go back to.

Arpeggio list, $4919-$4920: every tick the player steps to the next byte and adds it to the note as a signed number of semitones, so the voice cycles through a chord; $80 holds the current step, and $81 is followed by the position to go back to.

Arpeggio list, $4921-$4934: every tick the player steps to the next byte and adds it to the note as a signed number of semitones, so the voice cycles through a chord; $80 holds the current step, and $81 is followed by the position to go to. Here the $81 is followed by $14, a position past this list's end, so the steps run on through the list at $4935, whose own $81 00 then sends them back to the start of this one.

Vibrato settings, eight bytes each from $49C7, read with half of an instrument's byte 9 in Y: the tick it starts on, the tick from which it changes depth, a pointer to its up-and-down list, the interval in semitones, how far it divides that interval, the depth step, and the tick it stops changing. The tune's instruments use only the setting at 8, $49CF-$49D6, which runs on past $49D0 into the first sixteen bytes of the filter and pulse settings at $49D1, which no instrument reads as a filter or pulse setting, and its up-and-down list, $49D7, lies there too.

This load holds only its first 32 bytes, $4DE0-$4DFF: the rest comes with the play load, which writes over this one from $4E00 on (here $4E00 is DrawTitleCard).

DrawTitleCard: the loader calls this at $1108 once the last byte of The Sewers' title load is in, before it starts the tune and waits for Space or fire on either port. It relocates the title's scene pointers (once: TitleRelocateScenePointers at $51A2), sets up the bitmap screen ($140B) and clears the play window's bitmap and its colour copy at $0800 ($140E), then goes on into the renderer below with A = 1, so it draws area 1's scene, scene 2: the level's picture with its name beneath, in the play window beside the status panel. The two NOPs stand where Central Park's RenderScene loads the area from $A2 ($8A52), so A keeps the 1 that the PLA brings back.

records.s: two NOPs in place of RenderScene's LDA $A2: A is still 1, area 1

records.c: TitleRenderSceneForRoomInA, the title load's copy of Central Park's RenderSceneForRoomInA ($8A54 there), the same instructions with the title's own table addresses. It looks area A up in the area slots at $51E8: the low nibble of the second byte becomes the background colour ($D021 and $32), and the first byte is the scene, whose pointer it reads from $5228 (scenes 0 to 127) or $5328 (128 and up, which no title has). A pointer with bit 15 set returns at once; otherwise the pointer plus the scene base $51E5 is the scene to draw, in $02-$03.

TitleRenderSceneRecordTree, the copy of RenderSceneRecordTree ($8A86 there): sets the window to 30 cells across ($E7) and 18 down ($DC), the nesting depth $38 and the origin $1A-$1B to zero, and goes on into the dispatch loop.

TitleSceneRecordDispatchLoop, the copy of SceneRecordDispatchLoop ($8A96 there): reads the next placement of the composite at $02-$03. $FF ends a composite: at depth zero it returns; deeper, it pulls the parent's place and origin back off the stack, lowers the depth and steps past the placement that led in. Anything else is decoded (TitleDecodeSceneRecord).
TitleAdvanceSceneRecordAndContinue, the copy of AdvanceSceneRecordAndContinue ($8AB1 there): steps $02-$03 past the placement (TitleAdvanceSceneRecordPointer) and goes back to the dispatch loop.

TitleAdvanceSceneRecordPointer, a copy of the play code's AdvanceSceneRecordPointer ($8AB7 in Central Park): adds a placement's length to $02-$03: three bytes, one more when bit 6 of the second byte is set, and one for each colour swap that bits 5 and 6 of the third byte count.

TitleDecodeSceneRecord, the copy of DecodeSceneRecord ($8AD8 there): takes the placement's mirror flag (bit 7 of its second byte, into $E8), its column (the low six bits less 14, plus the origin $1A, into $25) and its row (the low five bits of the third byte less 14, plus $1B, into $26), and looks its scene up in the pointers at $5228. A composite (bit 15 clear) is entered: the origin and the place are pushed, the depth $38 goes up, and the dispatch loop goes on inside it with the placement's column and row as the new origin. A picture (bit 15 set) is drawn by TitleDrawScenePicture, its address in $04-$05.

TitleDrawScenePicture, the copy of the picture drawer that starts at $8B49 in Central Park (RenderUiSceneRecord there). The size byte gives the width (high nibble, $1C) and height (low nibble, $1D) in cells, and a picture wholly outside the window is skipped. It reads the placement's colour swaps, finds the picture's screen bytes and colour bytes after its bitmap bytes, works out where its first visible cell lands in the bitmap, screen RAM, colour RAM and the colour copy at $0800 (the engine's row tables at $1414, $142D, $1446 and $145F), then draws it cell by cell, row by row, clipped at the window's edges. Each cell's screen and colour bytes have the swaps applied (a nibble equal to a swap's low nibble takes its high nibble); its eight bitmap bytes are copied as they are, or, mirrored, in the reverse order of columns and through the pair-reversal table at $1200. A cell whose byte in the colour copy has any of its top three bits set is kept unless the new cell's colour byte is $20 or more, and with bit 4 of it set as well the engine's routine at $1411 merges the two.

TitleRelocateScenePointers, the copy of RelocateScenePointers ($8A0F there), which DrawTitleCard calls first: it subtracts the relocation word at $51E6 from each of the 3 scene pointers the header at $51E5 counts, then stores RTS ($60) over its own first instruction, so that it does nothing if called again. This snapshot was saved after it ran: the RTS is in place, and the $00 after it is the operand of the LDA #$00 that it replaced.
records.s: RTS: the LDA #$00 as loaded, overwritten at $51AF after the one run

records.c: Scene header: 3 scene pointers follow at $5228, which the one-time relocation at $51A2 adjusts by the word at $51E6; every pointer is an offset from this address, $51E5.
Relocation word, $0800 in this snapshot: TitleRelocateScenePointers subtracts it from each of the 3 scene pointers, then overwrites its own first instruction with RTS so that it never runs again.
The relocation word's high byte, which TitleRelocateScenePointers subtracts with the borrow from the low byte ($51C4 and $51DA).

32 two-byte area slots, $51E8-$5227: the scene that draws the area, then its background colour in the low nibble. 18 areas have a scene (area 0: scene 2, area 1: scene 2, area 2: scene 2, area 3: scene 2, area 4: scene 2, area 5: scene 2, area 6: scene 2, area 7: scene 2, area 8: scene 2, area 9: scene 2, area 10: scene 2, area 11: scene 2, area 12: scene 2, area 13: scene 2, area 14: scene 2, area 15: scene 2, area 16: scene 2, area 17: scene 2); $FF marks a slot no area uses. Every slot of the title's that is not $FF names scene 2: DrawTitleCard draws area 1 only, and the background colour it sets is 0.
The area slots plus 1, read at $4E11 with X at an area's slot: the area's background colour, in the low nibble.
Scene pointer 000: $804B, bit 15 set: a picture, at $5230, the offset plus the scene base $51E5.
The scene pointers plus 1, read and written at $4E29, $4EC0, $51C1 and $51C7 with the index at a pointer's low byte: the high byte of each pointer.
Scene pointer 001: $8916, bit 15 set: a picture, at $5AFB, the offset plus the scene base $51E5.
Scene pointer 002: $0D31, bit 15 clear: a composite scene, at $5F16, the offset plus the scene base $51E5.

One pointer more than the 3 the header counts, $1538: the relocation stops before it, so it keeps the value it was built with, and less the relocation word $0800 it is $5F1D, the byte just past the last scene, where a lone $FF closes the pool.

Scene 000, a picture 15 cells wide and 15 high, $5230-$5AFA: the size byte $FF (width in the high nibble), then 1800 bitmap bytes, 225 screen bytes and 225 colour bytes, eight, one and one for each cell.

Where the renderer's copy looks for the pointers of scenes 128 and up ($4E2E, $4EC5, $51CD and $51D4). The title has 3 scenes, so those instructions never run, and this byte is inside scene leaf 000 ($5230-$5AFA), whose bytes go on from here.
The same table plus 1, the high bytes ($4E31, $4EC8, $51D7 and $51DD): never read, as no title has a scene 128; this byte is inside scene leaf 000 ($5230-$5AFA), whose bytes go on from here.
title scene leaf 000 continued, $5630-$5A2F of $5230-$5AFA.
title scene leaf 000 continued, $5A30-$5AFA of $5230-$5AFA.

Scene 001, a picture 7 cells wide and 15 high, $5AFB-$5F15: the size byte $7F (width in the high nibble), then 840 bitmap bytes, 105 screen bytes and 105 colour bytes, eight, one and one for each cell.
title scene leaf 001 continued, $5EFB-$5F15 of $5AFB-$5F15.

Scene 002, a composite of 2 placed scenes, $5F16-$5F1C, ending with $FF. Each placement is the scene number, a byte whose bit 7 mirrors it and whose low six bits are its column plus 14, and a byte whose low five bits are its row plus 14 and whose bits 5-6 count colour swaps that follow (a byte each); bit 6 of the second byte adds one more byte. Scenes placed: 0, 1.
A lone $FF just past the last scene, where the extra pointer at $522E leads: read as a scene it would be a composite with nothing in it.
226 bytes of $FF, $5F1E-$5FFF, after the scene pool and up to the end of the title load: no instruction reads them.
